data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The safest protocol abandons the mutable workspace model in favor of a content-addressed Merkle-DAG where completed evidence is an ancestral node and reclamation only garbage-collects orphaned leaves.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The Merkle-DAG root pointer or naming index may still be mutable and subject to silent displacement even if the nodes are immutable.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"A bug in the orphan-detection algorithm could misidentify evidence ancestors, leading to reclamation of completed subtrees.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Deterministic replay may produce a different content hash due to unrecorded environmental dependencies such as library versions or CPU features.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The deterministic workspace is structured as a Merkle-DAG of side effects. Completed evidence is defined by its content hash; once written, it is immutable and globally addressable. Reclamation scans for orphaned unmerged leaves\u2014nodes with no descendant evidence root\u2014and removes only those. Silent displacement is structurally impossible because overwriting a content-addressed hash would change its address, making any displacement explicit rather than silent.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
